mission.title: Install and Configure Oracle Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE)
mission.description: Oracle Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE) is a managed Kubernetes service that simplifies the deployment and management of Kubernetes clusters on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. It provides a fully managed environment, allowing users to focus on application development rather than infrastructure management. Key trade-offs include reliance on Oracle's cloud services and potential vendor lock-in.

steps.title: Install the Oracle Cloud CLI
steps.description:
This step installs the Oracle Cloud Command Line Interface (CLI), which is necessary for managing Oracle Cloud resources.

```bash

curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oracle/oci-cli/master/scripts/install/install.sh

bash install.sh --accept-all-defaults

oci --version

```

> Download the installation script.
> Run the installation script with default settings.
> Verify the installation by checking the CLI version.

steps.title: Create an OKE Cluster
steps.description:
This step creates a new Kubernetes cluster in Oracle Cloud, specifying the version, node count, and region.

```bash

oci ce cluster create --compartment-id <your_compartment_id> --name my-cluster --kubernetes-version 1.30.2 --vcn-id <your_vcn_id> --node-pool-configuration '"nodePoolConfigurations": [{"name": "my-node-pool", "nodeShape": "VM.Standard2.1", "nodeCount": 3}]'

```

> Replace <your_compartment_id> and <your_vcn_id> with your actual IDs.

steps.title: Set Up Kubeconfig
steps.description:
This step configures your kubeconfig file to connect to the newly created OKE cluster.

```bash

oci ce cluster create-kubeconfig --cluster-id <your_cluster_id> --file $HOME/.kube/config --region <your_region>

```

> Replace <your_cluster_id> and <your_region> with your actual values.

steps.title: Verify Cluster Nodes
steps.description:
This step checks the status of the nodes in your Kubernetes cluster to ensure they are running.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> You should see the nodes listed with a status of 'Ready'.

steps.title: Post-Install Configuration
steps.description:
This step sets up autoscaling and monitoring for your cluster.

```bash

kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oracle/oci-cloud-controller-manager/main/deploy/oci-cloud-controller-manager.yaml

kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oracle/oci-cloud-controller-manager/main/deploy/monitoring.yaml

```

> Deploy the OCI Cloud Controller Manager.
> Deploy monitoring resources.

uninstall.title: Delete the OKE Cluster
uninstall.description:
This step removes the OKE cluster and all associated resources. Be aware that this will result in data loss.

```bash

oci ce cluster delete --cluster-id <your_cluster_id> --force --wait

```

> Replace <your_cluster_id> with your actual cluster ID.

uninstall.title: Remove the Oracle Cloud CLI
uninstall.description:
This step uninstalls the Oracle Cloud CLI from your system.

```bash

rm -rf ~/.oci

```

> Remove the OCI configuration directory.

upgrade.title: Upgrade the OKE Cluster
upgrade.description:
This step includes backing up your data, upgrading the cluster, and verifying the upgrade.

```bash

kubectl get all --all-namespaces > backup.yaml

oci ce cluster update --cluster-id <your_cluster_id> --kubernetes-version 1.30.2

kubectl get nodes

```

> Backup all resources in the cluster.
> Upgrade the cluster to the specified version.
> Verify that the nodes are running the new version.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Unable to connect to the server: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates an issue with the kubeconfig file or the cluster's API server certificate.

**Fix:**
Regenerate the kubeconfig file using the correct cluster ID and region.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Insufficient CPU resources available'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the requested resources exceed the available capacity in the specified region.

**Fix:**
Check the available shapes and adjust the node pool configuration accordingly.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Failed to create load balancer'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This can occur if the necessary permissions are not granted to the dynamic group.

**Fix:**
Ensure that the dynamic group has the required permissions to manage load balancers.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Node is not ready'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This may indicate that the node is still initializing or there are issues with the underlying infrastructure.

**Fix:**
Check the node status and logs for more details, and ensure that the underlying resources are healthy.

versionNotes.changes: Added support for new node shapes and improved integration with Oracle Cloud services.
versionNotes.deprecations: Deprecated support for Kubernetes versions below 1.28.
versionNotes.migrationSteps: Ensure that your workloads are compatible with the new features and test them in a staging environment before upgrading.

resolution.summary: You should see the output of 'kubectl get nodes' showing all nodes in 'Ready' status, confirming that the cluster is operational.

prerequisites.description: Ensure you have the necessary tools and resources before starting the installation.
